messages.body_plain:
Hi Kajia,

Yes, CODEX is implemented in R. We read in raw bam files using Rsamtools which is very fast. The normalization step might be RAM intensive depending on how many samples you have and the range of latent factors you want to choose from.

CODEX estimated both sample- and exon-wise latent factors iteratively and therefore it needs a decent number of samples--I've personally run CODEX with 30 samples. And yes, different batches can be processed together, although for maximized performance, it's suggested to be analyzed separately.

Let me know if there's any further question,
Yuchao

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuchao,

After trying your tool, we really like it.  But few things we want to find out if it is available.  First, We want to normalize the pooled samples once and when there is a new sample, we just want to call CNVs on the new sample based on the normalization on the pooled samples, instead of running the whole process all over again.  Is it doable?  For example, if we have few hundreds or even thousands of samples that we can pool together for normalization, but we only want to call CNVs on some new samples that are not in the pool.

It might be even better if you have a p-value or FDR to indicate the likelihood of having a CNV at the location is not by chance.  But its a plus, not a necessary improvement.

Thank you,
Kajia

messages.subject: Re: more questions about CODEX
messages.body_plain:
Hello Yvan,

Yes, you are correct. CODEX is originally designed for whole exome sequencing and not specifically for exon targeted sequencing. It analyzes each chromosome separately as do many other softwares. We do, however, have collaborations at UPENN where we adapt CODEX to call CNVs from targeted next-gen sequencing data. In this sense, we pulled the read depth across all chromosomes and normalize the genome-wide read depth matrix all at once.

I will try to come up with a version for exon targeted sequencing but essentially the code would look like getting coverage, gc content, mappability for targets on each chromosome, combine them together as one matrix (read depth) and vector (GC content, mappability) for the entire genome, and then run the QC, and normalization. For targeted sequencing, since there aren't too many targets in each gene, we use thresholding rather than CBS for CNV calling. Namely, take the log ratio of Y_qc divided by Yhat[[optK]] with optK being the optimal value of the number of latent factors.

For your question on the bed file, again, the error is due to the fact that CODEX doesn't work in a cross-chromosome fashion at this moment. However, for each chromosome--you are right--the bed file needs to be sorted with positions of targets in rising orders.

Thank you for all of your questions and suggestions--they certainly help us improve our software and understand the problem better. However, for your future contacts, could you email to the user group directly at codex_...@googlegroups.com (and cc me and Nancy if you wish)? This way, more users can see the questions and solutions.

I will keep you posted on the version of CODEX for targeted sequencing.

Cheers,
Yuchao

messages.subject_clean: more informations about my problem on CODEX package
messages.body_plain:
Hello Yvan,

Your codes are all fine and I do see reads mapped to the exonic regions you sent me using samtools. The reason you got 0 reads mapped by getcoverage() and therefore NaN read length is because all of your reads in your bam files are from the second read pair (or maybe it’s single end sequencing). CODEX extracts the first mate pair read and process from there:

  flag <- scanBamFlag(isDuplicate = FALSE, isUnmappedQuery = FALSE,

                      isFirstMateRead = TRUE)

  param <- ScanBamParam(which = which, what = what, flag = flag)

  bam <- scanBam(bamurl, param = param)[[1]]

I would suggest you check the details of you exon targeted sequencing and the pre-processing of your bam files (mapping etc). This is the first time I’ve seen this issue and the software has been used at UPENN campus quite extensively. Another option for you is to remove the red flag above and re-source your getcoverage() function. You will get reads mapped.

Cheers,

Yuchao

messages.subject_clean: A question of running codex on new samples without re-normalize all pooled samples
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuchao,

This is a way on how to manage adding the new samples.  So at the read depth computing step, we can save all pooled samples as a R object, and when we have new samples, we can compute the read depth of new samples and merge the two objects together and then precede to the next step. This would save users some time and provide some flexibility.  I think u can add it in your manual page.

Thanks,
Kajia
